correctness.rationale: For a two-row ladder L_n and 3<=k<=2n-3, every complement with >=k+2 vertices contains a disconnected k-subset by choosing an extreme-column vertex of induced degree at most two, giving the full skeleton below codimension one. Missing top facets correspond exactly to connected k-subsets; missing next-to-top faces correspond to deletion-robust (k+1)-subsets, which in a ladder are precisely full consecutive rung blocks, counted by b_{n,k}. Enumerating connected induced subsets by 3 column states and forbidding adjacent opposite singletons yields 2A and D recurrence with GF C(z,t)=zt(2+t+zt^2)/((1-z)^2(1-z(t+t^2)-z^2t^3)). The alternating binomial Euler identity yields beta_{n,k}=binom(2n-1,k-1)-[z^n t^k]C+b_{n,k}; Theorem 5.6 of Chandrakar et al. supplies the precisely matching pure shellability range, upgrading Euler to an integral top-dimensional sphere wedge. Independent direct connectivity/deletion-robust/cut-face checks covered every permitted k for n=3..7, including k=5 ranks 13,85,270,636 for n=4..7. Finite enumeration was not used to prove all-n classification.

Published high-girth and circular-ladder results do not cover ordinary path ladders in this range. Best-of-knowledge.
